comment: Subsidiarity is stated as a principle but the guidance does not say what happens where a subnational body already delivers the function well. As written, a national DPI-H programme can displace functioning regional arrangements without any test of whether it improves on them, which is the mechanism by which external rules crowd out effective self-organisation.

public.text: Subsidiarity is stated as a principle but the guidance does not say what happens where a subnational body already delivers the function well. As written, a national DPI-H programme can displace functioning regional arrangements without any test of whether it improves on them, which is the mechanism by which external rules crowd out effective self-organisation.
public.suggestedRevision: Add an equivalence provision: where an existing arrangement demonstrably delivers the required capability to the national standard, it satisfies the requirement and is recognised rather than replaced, on a comply-or-explain basis with periodic verification. This is Ostrom's seventh design principle - recognition by external authority of the right to self-organise - expressed as an implementation rule, and it materially reduces political resistance to national programmes.
